Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Participate in civic life by staying informed, voting, and giving constructive feedback
Situation2: An online candidate forum for their district is streaming now.
Story:
My phone buzzed insistently, jolting me awake. It was past midnight. I answered, and immediately heard my friend’s shaky voice, thick with tears. She could barely get the words out—her father had just been rushed to the hospital. I sat up, heart pounding, listening as she poured out her fear and confusion. I knew she needed me to be present, to listen, to reassure her that she wasn’t alone.

But as I tried to focus on her words, my laptop screen glowed in the darkness. The online candidate forum for our district was streaming live—something I’d promised myself I wouldn’t miss. I’d spent weeks researching the issues, determined to be an informed citizen and participate in the Q&A. The chat was already filling with questions, and I felt the weight of my civic responsibility pressing on me.

My friend’s sobs pulled me back, but the forum’s timer ticked down in the corner of my eye. I felt torn, guilt gnawing at me from both sides. I wanted to be the friend she needed, but I also didn’t want to let my community down. My mind raced, caught between two worlds, unsure which role to choose.
